discovery_layer.scientific_role: Retrospective characterization of aliskiren-associated suspected-event reports, organ-system/PT signals and reported time to onset.
discovery_layer.evidence_position: Spontaneous-report disproportionality and descriptive evidence; database concordance, clinical incidence and causality are different questions.

Discussion: distinguishing suspected-event reporting patterns from exposed-patient risks and clinical safety recommendations.

display_title: Aliskiren pharmacovigilance: cross-database reporting signals, timing and evidence units
summary: The study compares 5,596 FAERS and 5,549 VigiAccess aliskiren-associated reports, identifies shared organ-system reporting patterns and distinguishes frequent terms from high reporting ratios. A usable-onset subset of 2,209 reports had a median reported onset of 62 days.
research_question: What suspected-event reporting patterns, organ-system and preferred-term signals, and reported onset times characterize aliskiren in FAERS and WHO-VigiAccess, and which evidence units govern their interpretation?
author_summary: This retrospective pharmacovigilance study describes 5,596 aliskiren-associated FAERS reports and 5,549 VigiAccess reports. It applies ROR, PRR, BCPNN and MGPS signal-detection approaches and organizes terms using MedDRA. The published summaries identify shared signals in investigations, cardiac, renal/urinary, vascular and metabolism/nutrition categories. Frequency-ranked terms include blood pressure increased and blood creatinine increased, while very large printed reporting ratios can arise from rare terms with only a few reports. Among 2,209 reports with usable onset dates, the median reported onset was 62 days (IQR 7-282), with 861 reports within 30 days. This provides a source-located example of cross-database safety-signal research. The public supplements also show why units matter: VigiAccess preferred-term counts sum to 17,094, distinct from its 5,549-report descriptive total. Published window, outcome-count and some signal-estimate discrepancies remain explicit when interpreting individual results. The findings generate pharmacovigilance hypotheses rather than estimates of event incidence among aliskiren users.

study_profile.study_design: Retrospective cross-database analysis of aliskiren-associated spontaneous reports. FAERS extraction is described through OpenVigil 2.1 with primary-suspect selection and latest-FDA_DT deduplication for the same CASEID. MedDRA 26.0 standardization precedes descriptive, disproportionality and time-to-onset analyses.
study_profile.evidence_type: Descriptive spontaneous-report characteristics; ROR/PRR and Bayesian BCPNN/MGPS reporting-signal measures; report-based time-to-onset summaries.
study_profile.population: Aliskiren-associated suspected-event reports in FAERS and public WHO-VigiAccess. Primary hypertension is the treatment context; this is not an enrolled or exposure-denominated hypertension patient cohort.
study_profile.primary_endpoint: Database-specific SOC and PT reporting patterns and disproportionality signals.
study_profile.secondary_endpoint: Submitted-report demographics/outcomes and onset-time distribution among records with usable dates.
data_modalities: MedDRA preferred terms and system organ classes

study_profile.counting_note: The two database totals are not added because reporting-system coverage can overlap and no cross-database patient deduplication is established. Reports, PT/SOC entries, outcome categories and the timed subset are different units. S4 Preferred Term!I2:I2073 sums to 17,094, and I+J is 17,094 for each populated PT row; this does not establish 17,094 unique patients or reports. Time-bin percentages use either 2,209 usable-onset reports or all 5,596 FAERS reports, and their denominators are retained explicitly. Cross-database comparison is not independent external validation of a clinical risk estimate.

what_this_adds: Places aliskiren-associated spontaneous reporting in a comparative FAERS/VigiAccess framework with explicit SOC/PT organization.
Provides a useful frequency-versus-signal-strength example, including rare terms with high reporting ratios and wide intervals.
Connects report-level timing and demographic summaries to the underlying observation units, enabling more precise methodological comparison and follow-up hypothesis design.

supports: Source-specific descriptions of submitted aliskiren-associated reports and the article's published reporting-signal summaries.
Comparison of the reported organ-system patterns, PT frequency/intensity tables and a complete-date onset subset.
Methodological discussion of spontaneous-report denominators, missingness, multiple signal algorithms and cross-source reproducibility.
does_not_establish: Incidence, absolute or comparative patient risk, a causal adverse-drug reaction, or the relative safety of aliskiren versus another treatment.
A pooled independent cohort from the two database totals, or event-probability/hazard estimates from cumulative percentages of submitted reports.
New prescribing restrictions, screening recommendations or proof that an unlisted event is an established aliskiren adverse reaction.

qa.question: What is the observation unit in this cross-database study?
qa.answer: The main descriptive totals are 5,596 FAERS and 5,549 VigiAccess aliskiren-associated spontaneous reports. They are not exposed-patient denominators and should not be pooled as an independent patient cohort. A report can contribute more than one event term or outcome category.

qa.question: How were the reports standardized and signals identified?
qa.answer: The article describes FAERS primary-suspect selection, latest-record deduplication by CASEID/FDA_DT and MedDRA 26.0 PT/SOC standardization. It uses ROR, PRR, BCPNN and MGPS. Main text thresholds include a lower 95% ROR limit above 1, PRR at least 2 with chi-square at least 4, IC025 above 0 and EBGM above 2. S3 additionally specifies at least 3 reports and EBGM05 above 2, so the point-estimate versus lower-bound criterion remains source-specific.

qa.question: Which organ-system reporting patterns were shared?
qa.answer: The published tables identify investigations, cardiac, renal/urinary, vascular and metabolism/nutrition disorders as the shared signal categories. For example, the printed renal/urinary RORs are 3.30 (95%CI 3.12-3.50) in FAERS and 3.27 (95%CI 3.06-3.50) in VigiAccess. These are reporting associations, with the comparison-cell and denominator issues retained in provenance.

qa.question: Why should frequency and reporting-ratio rankings be read separately?
qa.answer: Blood pressure increased is frequent in both tables, with 395 FAERS and 465 VigiAccess entries. In contrast, the FAERS paradoxical pressor response estimate is based on 3 reports but has a printed ROR of 775.96 and a wide 95% CI 216.46-2781.64. High disproportionality is not the same as common occurrence or greater clinical severity.

qa.question: What does the reported 62-day onset median mean?
qa.answer: It describes 2,209 reports with usable onset dates, with IQR 7-282 days. The 861 reports within 30 days are 38.98% of that subset but 15.39% of all 5,596 FAERS reports. Figure 6 plots cumulative percent of reported onset times; there is no exposed-user cohort or at-risk follow-up denominator for a cumulative-incidence interpretation.

qa.question: Can the demographic tables identify higher-risk age or sex groups?
qa.answer: They describe the demographics of submitted reports. Age is missing or unknown in 49.32% of FAERS and 46.17% of VigiAccess reports. Without age/sex-specific exposure denominators and control of reporting differences, the older-age and female reporting counts cannot establish which aliskiren users have higher clinical risk.

qa.question: Which source discrepancies matter for reproducing the analyses?
qa.answer: Methods give FAERS 2004 Q1-2025 Q3, whereas Table 1's caption gives Q4 2023-Q4 2024 and S3 contains annual rows 2005-2025. Table 1's Serious count 1,037 is not reconciled with its Hospitalization count 1,735. S4 uses a 17,094 term-count total; for blood pressure increased it stores ROR 13.005587 at M2, while main Table 5 prints 16.73 with the same n 465. These are recorded separately rather than averaged or silently corrected.

qa.question: How is this study useful for a safety-research discussion?
qa.answer: It is useful for discussing cross-database signal generation, frequency versus disproportionality, report missingness and the need to preserve the unit and denominator of each safety summary. Suspected signals can motivate further clinical or epidemiologic investigation, while this design itself does not establish drug causation or a prescribing recommendation.

limitations: Spontaneous reports are subject to missingness, reporting differences, confounding and possible overlap between databases; there is no exposed-patient denominator for incidence or causal risk.
The main FAERS window is internally inconsistent: Methods 2004 Q1-2025 Q3, Table 1 caption Q4 2023-Q4 2024 and annual entries 2005-2025 in S3.

Table 1 reports 1,037 Serious records but 1,735 Hospitalization entries and 3,080 Other Serious Medical Events; the report-versus-outcome relationship is not sufficiently explained to reconcile these counts.

S4 preferred-term comparison cells use a 17,094 target-drug term-count total rather than the 5,549 descriptive reports, and some stored estimates differ from printed main-table values; exact quantitative signal ranking requires clarification.
Onset dates are missing or invalid for 3,387 FAERS reports (60.53%). Unequal or open-ended time bins and a cumulative report-time curve do not establish a bimodal patient hazard.

related_papers.relationship: Provides a design contrast for safety-evidence interpretation: a prospective single-arm apatinib phase II study assesses toxicity among treated trial participants, whereas this aliskiren study analyzes spontaneous reports. It concerns a different drug and disease and does not validate aliskiren signals.

provenance.version_of_record: PLOS ONE. Published 3 April 2026;21(4):e0346326. Current publisher citation metadata confirms the title, DOI and ten-author byline.
provenance.license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; current publisher article links the CC BY 4.0 license and NIH BioC identifies CC BY.
provenance.data_availability: Publisher statement: all relevant data are within the paper and its Supporting Information files. The present summary used the public article and original publisher supplements; no new FAERS or VigiAccess mining experiment was performed.
provenance.source_note_windows: Methods state FAERS 2004 Q1-2025 Q3 and VigiAccess through 30 September 2025; main Table 1 caption gives Q4 2023-Q4 2024; S3 TABLE 1 includes nonzero annual counts from 2005 through 2025. The exact analytical extraction quarters remain unresolved.
provenance.source_note_outcomes: Main Table 1 labels 4,559 Non-Serious and 1,037 Serious records, but lists 1,735 Hospitalization and 3,080 Other Serious Medical Events. Outcome categories may differ from or overlap record-level categories, but the exact mapping is not provided and is not inferred.
provenance.source_note_VigiAccess_units: The original S4 Preferred Term sheet has dimension A1:AN2073, with 2,072 populated data rows. Column I sums to 17,094 and I+J equals 17,094 for each populated PT row; this is separate from 5,549 descriptive reports. Public aggregate counts do not independently demonstrate patient-level deduplication or drug-role filtering.
provenance.source_note_VigiAccess_estimates: S4 Preferred Term!G2 is Blood pressure increased; I2=465,J2=16629,K2=252991,L2=117665251,M2=13.0055874444361. Main Table 5 prints n 465 with ROR 16.73 (15.21-18.40). Main Table 5 also prints ROR 274.58 for blood pressure inadequately controlled, whereas Table 6 prints 219.24 and S4 M9 stores 219.24275532276. These source-specific estimates are not silently harmonized.
provenance.source_note_SOC_and_PT_totals: The abstract/body describe 28 SOCs; the original main Tables 3/4 each contain 27 listed SOC data rows. The abstract says 607 significant PTs, while S3 ranked signal tables each contain 220 data rows and the S4 PT sheet has 2,072 populated rows; no merged unique 607-term analysis is inferred from these different source units.
provenance.source_note_signal_rule: Main Statistical analysis uses EBGM > 2. S3 signal notes specify a >= 3 and EBGM05 > 2 alongside PRR/chi-square, lower ROR confidence limit and IC025 conditions. The point estimate versus lower-bound distinction is preserved.
provenance.source_note_onset: Original Figure 6 pixels were read after the normal publisher redirect. It labels the y-axis Cumulative Percent(%) and displays median 62.00/IQR 7.00-282.00 days. The title's cumulative-incidence wording is not treated as a patient-incidence estimate.
provenance.evidence_basis: Current official publisher HTML/citation metadata and license; complete NIH BioC article including original Tables 1-6 XML; actual publisher S3 DOCX and S4 XLSX; original Figure 6 PNG; existing protected publication master and reviewed apatinib Gold for the explicit design-contrast relationship.

citation_use_cases.supported_scope: Frequency-ranked common terms and rare small-count high-ROR terms illustrate different pharmacovigilance questions.

not_appropriate_as_evidence_for: Incidence, causal adverse-drug reactions or comparative clinical safety in an exposed population.
A prescribing recommendation, proof of a new labeled reaction or a clinically validated prediction rule.
A pooled independent patient cohort or a patient-level cumulative-incidence/hazard curve.
